entrypoint_protocol: argv CLI; execute `python -m todo_cli`, pass commands and options as argv, and evaluate the process exit status and stdout
objective: Build a robust multi-file argv todo CLI with persistent local JSON state, add/list/done/stats commands, helpful errors, and real automated tests.
public_behavior_spec: The CLI is invoked from the candidate root as `python -m todo_cli [--data-file PATH] COMMAND ...`.
When `--data-file` is omitted, state is stored in `.todo.json` in the current working directory. Parent directories for an explicitly selected data file are created as needed.
`add TEXT` rejects empty or whitespace-only text. A successful add assigns a stable positive integer ID, persists the todo, and prints `Added todo ID: TEXT`.
`list` prints every todo in ascending ID order as `[ ] ID TEXT` for open todos and `[x] ID TEXT` for completed todos. An empty list prints `No todos.`.
`done ID` marks an existing todo complete, persists the change, and prints `Completed todo ID: TEXT`. Completing an already completed todo is idempotent and does not create another item.
`stats` prints counts containing `Total: N`, `Open: N`, and `Done: N`.
State remains available across separate process invocations and is represented by valid JSON containing durable todo IDs, text, and completion state.
IDs are not renumbered when a todo is completed, and newly added todos receive an unused increasing ID.

Invalid commands, invalid IDs, missing todos, empty text, and unreadable or malformed state produce a concise message beginning with `Error:` or an argparse-style usage error and return a nonzero exit status without a traceback.
`--help` returns zero and identifies the add, list, done, and stats commands.
The implementation uses only the Python standard library and is split into CLI, service/domain, and JSON storage modules.
The repository includes automated tests that exercise the CLI and persistent state using isolated temporary data.

public_tests.description: The argv entrypoint provides successful help covering every required command.
Listing a fresh explicitly selected state file reports that there are no todos.
Separate CLI processes share default local JSON state while add, list, done, and stats preserve IDs and completion state.
Whitespace-only todo text is rejected with a helpful message and nonzero status.
Completing an unknown ID fails clearly without exposing an internal traceback.
The submitted automated tests execute successfully using the standard-library unittest runner.

qualitative_rubric: CLI parsing is centralized and keeps presentation concerns separate from todo operations and persistence.
JSON storage validates loaded data, reports malformed or inaccessible state helpfully, and avoids silently discarding existing data.
Writes use a safe replacement strategy or comparable technique to reduce the risk of leaving truncated JSON.
Domain and storage code have clear interfaces, sensible names, type hints or equivalent documentation, and no unnecessary global mutable state.
Automated tests contain meaningful assertions for success, failure, and cross-process persistence rather than merely smoke-running code.
The implementation remains portable across current Python 3 environments and does not rely on network access, third-party packages, shell-specific syntax, or machine-specific paths.
stopping_condition: Stop when all required artifacts exist, every public executable test passes from a clean isolated working directory, persistent behavior is demonstrated across separate invocations, and the qualitative rubric has no critical robustness or test-quality deficiency.
